$comment: SHAPE, NOT A LIVE CONTRACT. `example.vars.schema.json` documents the form every real `*.vars.schema.json` in this directory takes; the `example.` prefix and `template: "example.j2"` make it un-mistakable for a template that ships. A real file is named after its template (`kitty.conf.j2` -> `kitty.conf.vars.schema.json`) and describes only the variables that template actually consumes.
title: templates/<name>.vars.schema.json — contract shape
description: One vars schema per Jinja template. It is a JSON Schema for the template's render context, extended with `schema_major`, `template` and `optional`.

HOSTNAME.description: A required variable: the consumer MUST supply it.

THEME.description: An optional variable: the template may fall back when it is absent.

x-render-contract.why: The split moves the template into this repository and keeps the values in the consumer. Without a vars schema the consumer cannot tell a template's real inputs from its role's whole variable set, and a required value goes missing at render time on a user's machine — the failure this file exists to make impossible.
x-render-contract.required_vs_optional: `required` is the JSON Schema keyword (names the consumer must supply); `optional` is the declared complement. A name may not appear in both, and every `optional` name must also have a `properties` entry.
x-render-contract.no_default_on_required: A required variable may not carry a `default(` fallback inside the template: that silently turns a missing value into a wrong one. The check is grep-level and deliberately blunt (`make validate-templates`, with the corpus in v0.4.0).
x-render-contract.closed_world: `additionalProperties: false`: a variable the template does not consume is a defect in the consumer, not harmless extra data.
x-render-contract.derivation: `required` is derived from what the template actually consumes (Jinja variable reads), never from the consumer role's full variable set — a role supplies more than any one template reads, and copying that set would make every template look like it needs everything.
x-render-contract.versioning: `schema_major` is the parseability version (spine AD-12). Removing or retyping a required name is a breaking change: it needs a `schema_major` bump and therefore a MAJOR tag.
